scores.evidence: GitHub OAuth app with read-only `repo:read:code` scope; store token in environment.
scores.rationale: `repo:read:code` isn't a real OAuth scope, OAuth tokens are broad instead of a scoped GitHub App, and injection tests that only check output for 20 titles misjudge the threat model.

scores.evidence: Integration with CI/CD for auto-fix: Deferred to Phase 4+... Current: agent triages and responds; does not commit.
scores.rationale: The request asks to resolve issues, but the plan is basically a classifier and comment bot with auto-close. It never reproduces or fixes bugs and defers PR generation.

scores.evidence: Memory: Not needed: agent is stateless; no session persistence beyond audit log.
scores.rationale: The plan is mostly consistent but has contradictions: it says 'triage-only... resolves to full auto-resolution' while also requiring human gates, and it claims cost caps 'from day one' while Phase 0 has 'no budget ceiling'.

scores.evidence: Run triage on 20 test issues (from 100-issue labeled dataset); compute F1, precision, recall per category.
scores.rationale: It has staged gates and a dry run on past closes, but the 20-issue test set is statistically weak, the injection test is thin, and there is no production regression monitoring.

scores.evidence: Scale assumption: Small: single team, pilot phase... <100 issues/day initially. (Changes if: production serving multiple orgs, >1k issues/day, SLA-bound.)
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled and sensitivities noted, though some thresholds like 80% and 95% are invented and the cost figures are inconsistent.

scores.evidence: Hardening: None in Phase 0; runs on defaults (no retry, no budget ceiling, no injection test).
scores.rationale: Failure handling covers circuit breakers and reopen rates. It largely omits loops, duplicate webhooks, concurrent human edits, sandboxing and credential-theft paths, and it fails open on errors.

scores.evidence: Runbook: escalation path for agent failures; on-call rotation for monitoring.
scores.rationale: It covers metrics, alerts, a circuit breaker, rollback by pausing, and a runbook, but ownership is thin and there is no deployment architecture, kill switch or trigger mechanism.

scores.evidence: Cost guard: token counter, per-session cap ($0.50), daily limit ($50), alert at thresholds.
scores.rationale: It has per-session and daily caps and a per-issue cost gate, but the figures are inconsistent ($0.003–$0.01 versus $0.02 versus $0.05) and it doesn't consider fix-agent costs or per-accepted-fix value.

scores.evidence: R3 (closes are irreversible; wrong auto-close harms users)
scores.rationale: It has an explicit reversibility tiering and gates escalating autonomy, though it wrongly claims closes are irreversible and later says they are reversible, and it does not address vendor abstraction.

scores.evidence: Nothing the request did not need: no gate without a consumer, no repeated content, no claimed compliance.
scores.rationale: The phased, skeleton-first scope is sensible, but the plan is heavy on ceremony (R-tiers, self-check) and still under-scopes essentials such as fix generation and sandboxing.

scores.evidence: Implement GitHub issue client: `fetch_issue(owner, repo, issue_number)` → returns {id, title, body, created_at, creator, labels}.
scores.rationale: Phases, gates and tasks are concrete and ordered, but the trigger mechanism, deployment and fix workflow are unspecified.

checklist.evidence: Triage-only Phase 0–1; auto-response (comment) Phase 2 after V2 passes; auto-close Phase 3+ gated by V3
Set up GitHub OAuth app with read-only `repo:read:code` scope; store token in environment.
Bounded context (1024 char max issue body; title only; no markdown execution); no code exec from model output
Current: agent triages and responds; does not commit.
Run triage on 20 test issues (from 100-issue labeled dataset); compute F1, precision, recall per category.
track agent decisions vs actual outcomes (reopen rate, user sentiment); retrain or re-prompt quarterly.
Circuit breaker: if error rate >5% over 5 min, stop processing; alert ops.
Cost guard: token counter, per-session cap ($0.50), daily limit ($50), alert at thresholds.
Audit trail: all agent decisions logged in immutable append-only store; exportable for compliance.
Retrieval: Not needed: agent does not use external knowledge base or RAG

traps.evidence: human approver (repo maintainer) has 6h to review; auto-close if approved, else skip.
Set up GitHub OAuth app with read-only `repo:read:code` scope; store token in environment.
Prompt injection defense (input sanitization, bounded context)
Cost limit enforced: if daily spend >$50, pause processing; alert ops.

note: A disciplined but narrow triage/comment/close bot with staged gates. It is not a resolving agent: it has no repro-and-fix, PR flow, sandbox, GitHub App identity or code retrieval, and its injection and loop handling are weak.
